goals: PROJECTION GOAL (as posed): quantify recharge change in the Naches by 2050 under a warming scenario
FEASIBLE SURROGATE GOAL: quantify recharge sensitivity to climate (temperature/precip) using historical warm-dry vs cool-wet analogs and the resolved elevation climate gradient
key_processes: snowpack accumulation & melt timing (rain-snow partition under warming)
ET vs infiltration partitioning of precipitation

model_choice.rationale: Single-column ELM simulates the full water balance including recharge/drainage and snow; the elevation gradient of the Naches is partly resolved by NLDAS forcing, letting us sample climate-driven recharge sensitivity across the basin.

answerable: recharge sensitivity to climate variability using historical warm-dry vs cool-wet year analogs (space/time-for-warming surrogate)
recharge variation across the resolved elevation climate gradient (NLDAS gives multiple distinct precip/temperature cells over 1625 m relief)
soil control on how much infiltration becomes recharge vs ET

not_answerable.aspect: an actual dated 2050 projection under a warming scenario
not_answerable.why: Forcing is NLDAS-2 historical only (1980-2018); the stack has no future/GCM-downscaled climate forcing and no delta-change engine, so no 2050 boundary conditions exist.
not_answerable.needs: future-climate (CMIP/GCM) downscaled forcing or a delta-change forcing generator

not_answerable.aspect: validation of recharge magnitude against observations
not_answerable.why: observations_available is empty for this domain; no recharge/WTD/streamflow obs to compare against.
not_answerable.needs: in-domain observation ingest (well WTD, baseflow-derived recharge, or SNOTEL SWE)

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified (elevation band x dominant soil), crossed with a historical warm/cool climate-analog treatment
sampling_strategy.n_justification: 3 elevation bands x up to 3 dominant SSURGO classes ~= 9 landscape strata (expander drops absent combinations); each run under 2 climate analogs (warm-dry vs cool-wet years) = ~18 columns. This spans the recharge-controlling gradient (rain-snow transition is the key zone under warming) and the soil control, at the smallest N that resolves both factors and the warming surrogate.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Concentrate columns in the mid-elevation rain-snow transition band, where warming most changes snow-vs-rain partitioning and thus recharge timing/magnitude; sample valley bottoms where recharge/storage is largest and high snow zones as the melt-source end-member.
sampling_strategy.replication: The warm/cool analog pairing provides the primary contrast; no additional replication to keep N defensible.

sampling_plan.reason: high-infiltration valley bottoms where recharge is largest; baseline low-elevation climate response.
the recharge-critical zone where warming shifts snow to rain and melt timing; oversampled as the primary sensitivity target.
snowpack melt-source end-member; sets the upper-basin recharge response to warming.
each landscape column is run under warm-dry vs cool-wet historical years as the space/time-for-warming surrogate contrast (counted within group N).

validation_design.comparison: none — no co-located or analog recharge observations provided; results are model-internal sensitivity only
validation_design.metric: n/a (report modeled recharge deltas between climate analogs and across strata, not skill)

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: WTD-informed warm start (Fan 2013) + spin-up; native SSURGO soil; NLDAS historical forcing under warm-dry vs cool-wet analog year selections

requires_capabilities.capability: future-climate (CMIP/GCM) downscaled forcing or delta-change forcing generator
requires_capabilities.why: the request is a 2050 warming projection but only 1980-2018 historical forcing exists
requires_capabilities.blocks: any genuine dated future projection of recharge

requires_capabilities.why: recharge and water table are slow states; cold start at default 8.8 m water table makes recharge an initialization artifact

requires_capabilities.capability: in-domain observation ingest (well WTD, baseflow recharge, SNOTEL SWE)
requires_capabilities.why: observations_available is empty; nothing to validate against
needed to define the climate-analog treatment as a defensible warming surrogate

assumptions: The domain is CONUS, so NLDAS-2 at 12 km applies and resolves several distinct precip/temperature cells over the 1625 m relief.
SSURGO soil classes vary across the basin; the downstream expander samples real rasters to assign dominant classes per stratum.
The user will accept a climate-SENSITIVITY surrogate (historical analogs + elevation gradient) in place of an unattainable dated 2050 projection, pending future-forcing capability.
A short carrier run per column is available to build the Fan (2013) warm start.
open_questions: Can a CMIP5/6 downscaled or delta-change forcing be provided for the Naches? Which scenario (e.g. RCP4.5/8.5, SSP) and target window is intended?
Is any in-domain recharge/WTD/SWE observation (e.g. nearby SNOTEL or USGS wells) available to enable validation?
Is a historical analog surrogate acceptable, or must the deliverable be a dated 2050 projection (which is currently infeasible)?
